questions.q: What does quantization actually change about a model?
options: The number of layers in the model
The attention pattern used during decode
The number of bits used to represent weights (and sometimes activations)
The tokenizer used to encode the prompt
questions.explain: Quantization reduces the precision used to store weights and activations — the architecture, layer count, and attention pattern stay exactly the same.

questions.q: Why does quantization specifically help with the decode phase of LLM inference?
options: Decode is compute-bound, and quantization adds more compute
Decode is memory-bound, and quantization reduces the bytes that must move through memory
Decode doesn't use the KV cache, so quantization only helps prefill
Quantization eliminates the need for a GPU during decode
questions.explain: Decode is memory-bound (Lesson 4) — the GPU spends its time moving weights and KV cache through memory. Lower-precision weights mean fewer bytes to move per step.

questions.q: What is the main practical difference between PTQ and QAT?
options: PTQ requires a full training run; QAT does not
QAT quantizes a model after training with no further steps
PTQ quantizes an already-trained model using a calibration set, with no retraining; QAT simulates quantization during training
There is no difference — they are two names for the same process
questions.explain: PTQ is applied after training using a small calibration set and requires no retraining. QAT simulates the precision loss during training so the model's weights adapt to it.

questions.q: Why is per-channel (or group-wise) quantization generally preferred over per-tensor quantization?
options: It uses fewer bits overall, making the model smaller
It preserves more accuracy by giving each channel or group its own scale factor, at a small metadata cost
It removes the need for a calibration set entirely
It is required for every GPU regardless of model size
questions.explain: Using a separate scale per output channel or small weight group captures local variation in magnitude far better than one scale for an entire tensor, at only a small metadata overhead.

questions.q: What makes outlier values a particular challenge for quantization?
options: Outliers don't exist in neural network weights
A small number of unusually large-magnitude values can badly distort a narrow quantized range if handled naively
Outliers only appear in QAT, never in PTQ
GPUs cannot process outlier values at all
questions.explain: A handful of large-magnitude weights or activations can dominate a narrow quantization range if not handled carefully, which is why most serious quantization methods exist largely to manage outliers well.
